title: One Volcano Pumped 17 Million Tons of Gas Into the Sky and Cooled Earth

scenes.text: In 1991, one volcano cooled the entire planet.
Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines blew on June fifteenth.
Its ash column rose about 25 miles into the sky.
It sent about 17 million tons of sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere.
That gas spread around the world and reflected sunlight back to space.
Global temperatures dropped about half a degree for two years.

description:
On 15 June 1991 Mount Pinatubo erupted, sending an ash column about 25 miles high and roughly 17 million tons of sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere.
The gas formed a haze that reflected sunlight, and global temperatures dipped by about half a degree Celsius for around two years.
One volcano, one planet. What else could change the climate that fast? Tell us.
first_comment: Sunsets around the world turned unusually red for months afterward. Did your grandparents ever mention it?
